A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPA/T6 research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v4 reports original language-model pretraining, downstream benchmark evaluations, ablations and FlashTPA decoding measurements.

after.justification: v5 retains original pretraining, downstream evaluation, ablation and decoding-speed results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v5 Algorithm 2 explicitly extends the rank-1 FlashTPA reference procedure to general key/value ranks with masking, blockwise online softmax and block value mixing. v4 already discussed higher-rank extensions and supplied online rank-1 decoding. The TPA/T6 architecture, objectives and benchmarked rank-1 Triton kernel remain unchanged.

E1.justification: FineWeb-Edu pretraining, the nine downstream benchmark tasks and the decoding test scenarios remain the same. The added large-model FLOP examples are analytical calculations, not newly evaluated datasets or domains.

E2.justification: The language-model comparisons retain MHA, MQA, GQA and MLA, and decoding comparisons retain their corresponding optimized implementations. No comparator membership changes occur in retained experiments; Qwen is only an added citation.

E3.justification: The stated hyperparameters, hardware, model configurations, zero-/two-shot evaluation, metrics and decoding benchmark settings are retained. v5 newly describes pretraining as 50B tokens over one epoch, but does not establish a changed training budget or rerun.

E4.justification: v4 Table 5's medium-model third-order TPA evaluation is removed, while the small-model test remains in v5 Table 4. The non-contextual-factor, rank and learning-rate ablations, together with decoding-scaling analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed/run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v5 checklist item 7 explains the omission of error bars through computational expense, without adding uncertainty estimates or changing statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Every retained empirical table matches numerically, allowing equivalent rounding, and plotted results match. Removed v4 Table 5 reported medium third-order TPA averages of 49.28% zero-shot and 50.98% two-shot. v5 also adds worked analytical cost values in Appendix A.4, not measured performance improvements.

T1.justification: v5 substantially expands decoding analysis from attention-only costs to projection-inclusive comparisons, parameter counts, tiled-memory bounds and additional rank/model-size cases. Section 4.2 also corrects GQA reconstruction by scaling group masks by G to cancel the 1/G prefactor. The RoPE theorems and their proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about contextual factorization, T6, reduced KV storage, RoPE compatibility, competitive model quality and efficient long-sequence decoding.

C2.justification: v5 adds a limitation concerning generalization to other modalities and explains why error bars are omitted. Appendix A.4 adds interpretations of projection overhead and rank-dependent efficiency across larger configurations. Existing empirical interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds the explicit 50B-token/one-epoch description, fuller general-rank decoding instructions, software/data license information and additional code/data access instructions. The project link is updated; existing optimizer, hardware and architecture settings are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds the Qwen technical report and names Qwen as another compatible architecture in the introduction. The remaining cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v5 promotes the non-contextual-attention discussion from Appendix A into Section 4, removes the redundant architecture recap, and extensively rewrites and consolidates the computational appendices. It also adds acknowledgements, limitations and a reporting checklist, with author/affiliation edits.

P2.justification: The NeurIPS format substantially changes typography, spacing and placement of figures, tables and algorithms. Figures 7 and 8 now share a page, Figure 6 is integrated into the rewritten analysis with a revised caption, and appendix tables are consolidated. Plot content is retained; one empirical table is removed.

improvement.justification: The corrected GQA reconstruction, clearer computational exposition and additional reproducibility and limitation disclosures provide a limited overall improvement. The empirical foundation is largely unchanged, and removing the medium third-order TPA results slightly reduces supporting evidence. These gains improve technical clarity without substantially strengthening experimental validation.
